# SOOS — Multi-Agent Delegation (MAD)
# draft-sato-soos-mad-04
# https://soosproject.ai/drafts/mad/llms.txt
# Author: Tom Sato / MyAuberge K.K.
# Last updated: September 4, 2026

---

## SECTION 1 — Canonical One-Liner

MAD (Multi-Agent Delegation) is the kernel-enforced delegation and cluster governance protocol for concurrent SOOS agent sessions. It governs the full lifecycle of a multi-agent delegation tree: how it is created (SACR -- Sub-Agent Composition Record), how it operates (INV-4 Narrowing, hub-only communication constraint, cluster coordination), and how it ends (R-1 through R-8 revocation with full completion-state and cascade-behavior specification). Version -04 adds R-8 (Compromise), an eighth revocation trigger class with no timeout-based recovery path, and the security analysis of the denial-of-service surface that property creates.

MAD is NOT a general-purpose authorization framework, a token-passing protocol, or a scoping mechanism for API access.

---

## SECTION 2 — Problem Statement

Without MAD, your multi-agent system has no standardized way to:

- Produce a kernel-witnessed record of sub-agent spawning -- without SACR, sub-agent creation is an unaudited LLM API call with a scoped system prompt; SACR provides a kernel-signed, GAR-recorded composition event (ALE-SPAWN-01) before the sub-agent executes its first action
- Enforce a tool-subset invariant at spawn time -- without it, a spawning agent can grant a sub-agent broader tool access than it itself holds; the GEC atomically validates this at SACR issuance
- Prevent ungoverned inter-sub-agent coordination -- sub-agents that communicate directly create state changes invisible to the kernel; hub-only requires all coordination to route through the kernel-governed hub
- Reconstruct a delegation tree across GEC boundaries without full audit-log disclosure between domains -- XPID chaining provides this
- Give per-trigger normative depth to revocation, including the one trigger class with no recovery window -- R-8 (Compromise) closes a mapping gap the Mandate Lifecycle Events (MLE) profile's `reason: compromise` value had exposed, and names the denial-of-service tradeoff that trigger's urgency necessarily creates

---

## SECTION 3 — Key Normative Concepts

SACR (Sub-Agent Composition Record):
   The kernel-issued record governing Mechanism B sub-agent spawning. Issued by the GEC (not the agent) before the sub-agent executes its first action. Key fields: sacr_id (UUID v4), parent_assignment_id, parent_session_id, parent_mandate_id, parent_xpid, ephemeral_kia_ref (UUID v4, session-scoped), scope_constraints (tool_subset, cedar_action_subset, resource_envelope, so_type_scope), can_decompose (boolean, default false), max_spawn_depth (integer, strictly decrements per recursion level), hub_only (boolean, default true), replan_authority (NONE/BOUNDED/AUTONOMOUS, default NONE), sacr_signature (GEC Ed25519). Committed to GAR as ALE-SPAWN-01 before sub-agent execution. Distinct from Assignment (which governs what the sub-agent may do once it exists): SACR governs how it comes to exist.

ephemeral_kia_ref:
   A session-scoped identity (UUID v4) issued by the GEC at SACR issuance for Mechanism B sub-agents. Not a persistent Party Registry entry. Valid only for the duration of the spawned sub-agent's session. Retired on session close (ALE-SPAWN-04: EPHEMERAL_IDENTITY_EXPIRED). An Assignment's assigned_agent_id for Mechanism B MUST equal the SACR's ephemeral_kia_ref.

can_decompose / max_spawn_depth:
   can_decompose: boolean, default false. May the spawned sub-agent itself spawn further children? A sub-agent with can_decompose: false MUST NOT call gec.spawnSubAgent(). max_spawn_depth: integer, strictly decrements at each recursive spawn (parent's max_spawn_depth - 1 = child's ceiling). Value 0 = leaf; MUST NOT spawn. CONF-MAD-19: parent MUST NOT grant max_spawn_depth greater than (parent's own - 1).

hub_only:
   Boolean, default true. Sub-agents with hub_only: true MUST NOT send messages, state updates, or coordination signals directly to sibling sub-agents (CONF-MAD-HUB-01). The GEC enforces this via Cedar context.hub_only_active and by blocking Action::"DirectSubAgentComm" (CONF-MAD-HUB-03). Override requires hub_only: false in SACR AND explicit Cedar PERMIT AND a DIRECT_COMM_PERMITTED event committed to GAR. hub_only: false in a SACR issued by a hub_only: true parent is a conformance violation (CONF-MAD-HUB-04).

Sub-agent XPID:
   Derived as UUID5(KIA_XPID_NAMESPACE, parent_xpid + ':' + sacr_id) per Section 6.1. Provides a stable, derivation-based cross-cluster sub-agent identifier chaining from root orchestrator to leaf sub-agent. Recorded in ALE-SPAWN-01 and in every GAR governance span as soos.governance.xpid. Cross-cluster verification: receiving GEC obtains the SACR from the originating GEC, recomputes the XPID, verifies the match (CONF-MAD-XPID-01, -02).

SACR Registry:
   A kernel-internal lookup of active SACRs by session_id, used for hub-only enforcement and cross-cluster XPID verification. Rebuilt from committed ALE-SPAWN-01 events on kernel restart before any sub-agent session may execute (CONF-MAD-22).

R-1 through R-8 (full normative specs):
   R-1 (CAP Tier 0-A): completion PARTIAL always; cascade FULL; human reauth required; all SACRs voided, ephemeral refs retired immediately.
   R-2 (Scope Boundary): completion CLEAN (if Cedar DENY at Step 1 before execution) / PARTIAL (if post-execution) / UNKNOWN (if execution state unknown); cascade FULL; human reauth required.
   R-3 (Non-Response): completion UNKNOWN always (treated as PARTIAL per INV-15); cascade SELECTIVE (responsive descendants continue); operator may reauth + must notify principal.
   R-4 (Irreversible Threshold): completion CLEAN (if halted before action) / PARTIAL (if post-irreversible-action); cascade FULL; human reauth required.
   R-5 (Scheduled Rotation): completion CLEAN (if natural breakpoint reached) / PARTIAL; cascade NONE (session-specific); operator may reauth; natural breakpoint wait required (CONF-MAD-R5-01).
   R-6 (Operator Override): completion CLEAN/PARTIAL; cascade per revocation_scope field; operator may reauth + must notify principal.
   R-7 (DEADLOCK): completion UNKNOWN always; cascade ALL participating sessions simultaneously; human reauth required; ephemeral refs retained pending resolution or timeout.
   R-8 (Compromise, NEW in -04): trigger is a suspected or confirmed external attack on a mandate or its credential, detected via KIA reattestation failure, CAEP RISC signal, or operator report. GEC MUST halt the session immediately -- no natural-breakpoint wait, unlike every other trigger. Completion PARTIAL or UNKNOWN, never CLEAN. Cascade: full CASCADE_TO_DESCENDANTS, mirroring R-1, since a compromised mandate's authority to have issued any descendant is itself in question. Continuation: human principal MUST reauthorize; operator MUST NOT reuse the compromised credential or any credential derived from the same key material; GAR MUST record CONTINUATION_AWAITING_PRINCIPAL until the principal acts. Routes to HEM_TIER0_OBSERVED (HEM Class 6), the same escalation class as R-1. All SACRs issued by the revoked session and its descendants are voided simultaneously; ALE-SPAWN-04 emitted for each retired ephemeral identity with completion_state: PARTIAL.

R-8's structural difference from every other trigger:
   R-8 has no timeout-and-recover mechanism analogous to R-7's deadlock_timeout -- a compromise finding is treated as too urgent to wait on. This is a deliberate design choice given the threat model, but it creates an asymmetric attack surface documented in Section 15.12 (see below): an entity able to inject a false detection_source signal can trigger an unconditional, immediately-cascading revocation of a legitimate session and its entire descendant tree, with no auto-recovery window to bound the damage.

Completion State Matrix (Table 1 in Section 7.9):
   R-1: PARTIAL always. R-2: CLEAN (Cedar DENY Step 1) / PARTIAL / UNKNOWN. R-3: UNKNOWN always. R-4: CLEAN (pre-action) / PARTIAL. R-5: CLEAN (natural breakpoint) / PARTIAL. R-6: CLEAN (natural breakpoint) / PARTIAL. R-7: UNKNOWN always. R-8: PARTIAL (if in-flight completion state determinable) / UNKNOWN (if not) -- never CLEAN.

Cascade Behavior Matrix (Table 2 in Section 7.10):
   R-1, R-2, R-4, R-8: full CASCADE_TO_DESCENDANTS always. R-3: selective, responsive descendants continue. R-5: none (session-specific). R-6: per revocation_scope field. R-7: all participating sessions simultaneously.

Terms carried forward from MAD-02/-03 (no changes in -04):
   INV-4 (Narrowing Property), INV-15 (UNKNOWN = PARTIAL), INV-16 (completion_state REQUIRED in GAR on revocation), MANDATE_HOLD, DEADLOCK, Cluster state machine (ACTIVE/CLUSTER_BLOCKED/MANDATE_HOLD/DEADLOCK/TERMINATED), cascade_timeout, five cluster collision problems, BUDGET_TRANSFER, ALE-013 through ALE-016.

---

## SECTION 4 — Relationship to Adjacent Standards

KIA (draft-sato-soos-kia):
   Sub-agent XPID derivation (Section 6.1) uses the KIA XPID namespace and derivation scheme. The ephemeral_kia_ref in SACR is a session-scoped identity distinct from a persistent KIA Party Registry entry but derived under the same kernel identity infrastructure. R-8's KIA_REATTESTATION_FAILURE detection source is a direct integration point: MAD does not re-derive attestation logic, it consumes KIA's reattestation result as one of R-8's three detection sources.

HEM (draft-sato-soos-hem):
   Section 15.8 normatively references HEM-PRE-2 (pre-action confirmation for irreversible actions) as the cascade timing attack defense mechanism. HEM_MULTI_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED fires on R-7 (DEADLOCK). HEM_TIER0_OBSERVED (HEM Class 6) fires on both R-1 and R-8 -- the two triggers that route to the highest-authority principal. HEM-DIV-1 is referenced for sub-agents with replan_authority: BOUNDED, for deviation surfacing.

GAR (draft-sato-soos-gar):
   ALE-SPAWN-01 through ALE-SPAWN-04 registered in MAD's IANA section. Sub-agent XPID recorded as soos.governance.xpid in every GAR governance span. HUB_ONLY_VIOLATION, DIRECT_COMM_PERMITTED, IRREVERSIBLE_THRESHOLD_REACHED, SCHEDULED_ROTATION_INITIATED, SESSION_REVOKED_BY_OPERATOR, SACR_REGISTRY_REBUILT, and COMPROMISE_REVOCATION (new in -04, for R-8) are kernel events recorded in GAR.

Mandate Lifecycle Events (MLE):
   A SOOS-adjacent companion profile, not yet submitted as its own draft. Its reason: compromise value had no corresponding R-code in MAD prior to -04; R-8 closes that specific mapping gap. This is an internal cross-reference, not a Datatracker dependency.

DR-SPAWN-01 (June 19, 2026):
   Source document for SACR design (Section 4), hub-only constraint (OQ-SPAWN-06 resolution), tool-subset invariant (Section 5.1), spawn-depth invariant (Section 5.2), and can_decompose/max_spawn_depth/replan_authority Assignment extensions.

DR-MAD-REC-01 (June 4, 2026):
   Source document for the full R-1 through R-7 per-trigger normative specifications in Section 7. R-8 was added in -04, surfaced independently while mapping this taxonomy onto the MLE profile -- not sourced from DR-MAD-REC-01 itself.

RFC 8693 (OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange):
   MAD profiles Token Exchange for sub-mandate issuance; SACR is the kernel-layer primitive sub-mandate issuance depends on.

draft-ietf-oauth-transaction-tokens (Txn-Tokens):
   Short-lived, signed JWTs propagating user identity, workload identity, and authorization context through a call chain -- structurally adjacent to MAD's mandate-chain model.

AuthZEN 1.0 (OpenID Foundation):
   Defines the Policy Enforcement Point / Policy Decision Point separation model -- a standardized API for external policy decisions independent of the agent process, relevant to how a MAD-conformant GEC's Cedar evaluation could be externalized.

---

## SECTION 5 — Normative SOOS Cross-References

Versions below are those cited by MAD-04 as of its submission.

This draft depends on:
   IDP (draft-sato-soos-idp-05) -- IDP declared intent for SACR tool-subset and replan_authority; HEM-DIV-1 triggers on IDP divergence
   HEM (draft-sato-soos-hem-06) -- CLUSTER_CASCADE_ALERT; HEM_MULTI_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED; HEM_TIER0_OBSERVED for R-1/R-8; HEM-PRE-2 for irreversible action cascade defense
   MJWT (draft-sato-soos-mjwt-05) -- sub-mandate issuance; BUDGET_TRANSFER MJWT reissuance; continuation mandate predecessor_mandate_id
   KIA (draft-sato-soos-kia-06) -- XPID derivation namespace; ephemeral_kia_ref issuance; cross-cluster GEC Manifest verification; R-8's KIA_REATTESTATION_FAILURE detection source
   SOV (draft-sato-soos-sov-03) -- Sovereign Object instances cluster agents act on
   GAR (draft-sato-soos-gar-07) -- ALE-013 through ALE-016 (unchanged); ALE-SPAWN-01 through ALE-SPAWN-04; hub, R-trigger, and COMPROMISE_REVOCATION events

The following drafts depend on this draft:
   CAP (draft-sato-soos-cap-05) -- CAP applies per delegation level; R-1 trigger is a CAP Tier 0-A violation
   AEP (draft-sato-soos-aep-03) -- AEP session lifecycle defers to MAD Section 3.6 for revocation procedure (SA-09)
   AOP (draft-sato-soos-aop-02) -- Mission Plan SO / Mission Status SO orchestration coordinates with MAD for multi-agent sub-goal assignment
   CAP-RRS (draft-sato-soos-cap-rrs-03), PT (draft-sato-soos-pt-03), FAIP (draft-sato-soos-faip-02) -- delegation-tree-scoped governance and analytics

Version history: -02 (INV-4 Narrowing, cluster coordination, R-1 through R-7 taxonomy named but not fully specified). -03 added SACR, the hub-only constraint, XPID cross-cluster integration, and full per-trigger normative depth (completion state and cascade behavior matrices) for R-1 through R-7 -- but shipped with a literal bracket placeholder instead of real BCP14 requirement-levels boilerplate, a defect not caught until -04. -04 adds R-8 (Compromise) -- surfaced while mapping MAD's taxonomy onto the Mandate Lifecycle Events profile's reason: compromise value, which had no R-code counterpart -- reconstructs the missing BCP14 boilerplate from -02's original text, and adds Section 15.12 documenting the denial-of-service surface R-8's no-recovery-window design necessarily creates, with a normative signal-verification requirement as mitigation.
